input:
A second label does not establish a second object. Mott and Venn put the distinction plainly: “A copied label is not a second sample.”[1, p. 46] Their chapter asks readers to count the samples themselves rather than treating each label as an additional sample.

1. Mott C, Venn A. Tray maps. In: Orr J, ed. Manuals for Sample Rooms. Talmer Press; 2021:41–52.

facts.text: Chapter record: Ceri Mott and Aro Venn; Tray maps; in Manuals for Sample Rooms, edited by Jori Orr; Talmer Press; 2021; pages 41–52.
Page 46 says exactly “A copied label is not a second sample.”
The chapter instructs readers to count physical samples rather than counting labels as though every label identifies an additional sample.
